system.name: LM-DESIGN
system.one_liner: Reprograms a sequence-based protein language model into a structure-based protein designer with a lightweight structural adapter and iterative refinement.

content.variant_note: a structure encoder and a protein language model decoder joined by a structural adapter, with a problem case study and the two background families drawn beside it
content.argues: A protein language model with a structural adapter and iterative refinement designs sequences for a fold better than purely structure-based models, especially in flexible, structurally non-deterministic regions.
content.subject: Case study and evidence, the two model families with their data sizes, and the LM-DESIGN architecture with its refinement loop.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw the two model families you join as small background boxes with their own tints and data-size badges, then reuse those tints inside one large shadowed overview panel so the new model reads as their join; add a long return arrow with a loop icon for iterative inference.

summary: LM-DESIGN turns a sequence-based protein language model (pLM) into a designer for a given fold by adding a lightweight structural adapter and refining the sequence iteratively. Figure 1 is a six-panel overview. A to C present the problem: a pLDDT-coloured kinase with a flexible activation loop, an alignment where ProteinMPNN produces invalid repeats, and a plot of pLM refinement. D and E show the two background families, structure-based design models trained on CATH structures (pink) and pLMs trained on UniRef-50 sequences (green), with their sizes. Panel F, the largest, joins them: a structure encoder feeds an adapter inside the pLM decoder, and a return arrow marked x T refines the sequence.
summary_zh: LM-DESIGN 给序列蛋白语言模型加入轻量结构适配器，并迭代精修序列。图 1 共六个面板：A 到 C 展示激酶活化环的问题与初步实验，D 和 E 画出两类已有模型及其数据规模，F 是结构编码器、带适配器的解码器和 ×T 迭代回路。
notes: The pre-screen listed only model-anatomy; side-by-side-contrast (problem then fix: A-C diagnose, D-E show two families, F is the remedy) and concept-schematic (A-C) were added. The digest suggests that A and B form one pasted bitmap, the plot C another, and the shadowed frame of F a third; this is inferred from placed sizes. The bypass line around the structural adapter has no label, so no role is given. The sequence strings in F may be illustrative, hence real_values null.
